gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-zen-kaku-gothic-new: Ruler-straight and loosely paced, Bruno Ace sets each character on its own beat, with counters that never quite close up. Bruno Ace is built to announce; Zen Kaku Gothic New is built to be read.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-didact-gothic: Wide-spaced and a bit futuristic, Bruno Ace SC strings its letters out like beads. Didact Gothic follows with strokes of matching weight and no closed-up bowls, so the eye slides from one to the other.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-finlandica: Beaded, open, and unmistakably showy: that is Bruno Ace SC. Its spread-out letters earn their keep big and brief, while Finlandica keeps a plain sans outline you could trace with a finger.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-kantumruy-pro: Kantumruy Pro keeps its e wide open to the right and has no hairlines or swells anywhere in its sans-serif letters. Bruno Ace SC above it supplies the spaced-out, showy edge.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-koho: Expressive and a touch theatrical, Bruno Ace SC spaces its letters like beads. It does best at announcing, while KoHo, a sans with wide c apertures, does best at quietly carrying the words.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-m-plus-rounded-1c: Letters strung out like beads on a thread. Bruno Ace SC keeps its strokes uniform as a fixed pen, while M PLUS Rounded 1c, a sans-serif, lets its terminals stop short of curling back.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-noto-sans-cypriot: Open-mouthed and widely spaced, Bruno Ace SC looks like it was traced with a single pen thickness. It is made to stand out, while Noto Sans Cypriot, a sans-serif with an e that opens up, is made to be followed.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-tuffy: Showy, spaced, and bead-strung: Bruno Ace SC makes an entrance. Its strongest quality is the contrast with Tuffy, a plain sans sketched in one pencil pressure with a widely parted s.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-clash-grotesk: Cherry Swash arrives with a horseshoe c and diagonals as heavy as its verticals. Clash Grotesk, a plain sans with no thick-and-thin modulation at all, gives that swagger something level to stand against.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-bai-jamjuree: Cherry Swash swings a horseshoe-wide c. Cherry Swash is the one with weight in its diagonals and a loud presence, while Bai Jamjuree, a sans-serif, does its best work staying light and unpinched in round letters.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-national-park: Chunky display swagger over a tidy, rounded base. National Park keeps its pen pressure and angle constant, so a long stretch of text moves along smoothly while Cherry Swash holds the headline.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-tenor-sans: Horseshoe curves, heavy diagonals, plenty of nerve. Give Cherry Swash the bigger size, and let Tenor Sans, with stems a little heavier than its hairlines, take a quieter size below.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-albert-sans: Ruler-straight strokes, gaps you could drive through. Happy Monkey holds one line weight all the way through, and Albert Sans, a professional face, keeps its apertures open at tiny sizes.
